newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - Baden Wuertt. CPI up 0.2 pct m/m.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Baden Wuertt. CPI up 0.2 pct m/m.

text.p: The following are views expressed by economists after the German state of Baden Wuerttemberg reported a rise in December consumer prices of 0.2 percent month on month and 1.2 percent year on year.
The state of Hesse earlier reported an increase for December of 0.3 percent and a year on year increase of 1.4 percent:
GERTRUD TRAUD, BANK JULIUS BAER, FRANKFURT:
"The figures out of Hesse were slightly above our expectations. We had expected 0.2 percent. But the Baden Wuerrtemberg figures were as expected."

"The Hesse figure shows that raw material prices had risen a bit, but not excessively. If we get 0.2 percent out of North Rhine-Westphalia, the biggest state, then we can expect a figure of 0.2 percent for the whole of West Germany, as expected," said Traud.

ARMIN KAYSER, ECONOMIST AT SBC BANK IN FRANKFURT "The notable rise in the Hesse data, and the month-on-month rise in Baden-Wuerttemberg do not change the outlook for inflation to remain at a low level. We have a situation where inflation is at a historic low."

NORBERT BRAEMS, BZW DEUTSCHLAND, FRANKFURT "The figures are in line with our expectations, the market had also expected monthly increases of 0.2 or 0.3 percent. The increase is caused by gains in the price of personal goods and services like package holidays and hotel accommodation. But it's a seasonal effect and there is no change in the inflation which will remain fairly low year-on-year. We expect inflation will be 1.7 or 1.6 percent for 1997."
